steps.text: Combine onion, vinegar, oil, garlic, salt, and pepper in a large resealable plastic bag. Add lamb chops; coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat.
Remove lamb from marinade and leave any onions on that are sticking to the chops; discard marinade. Wrap exposed ends of bones with aluminum foil to keep them from burning.

Cook lamb chops on the preheated grill until grill marks appear and to desired doneness, about 3 minutes per side for medium. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should register 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Grilled Lamb Chops
raw_recipe.description: These grilled lamb chops are marinated in a flavorful garlic marinade, then seared on a hot grill until tender and juicy for a delicious summer meal.

video.description: Easy recipe for lamb chops when you’re looking forward to using your grill! Perfect for the warmer months and goes perfectly with a side of vegetables and mashed potatoes!

review.reviewBody:
Hi! This is Noor and I would just like to add a comment about the recipe. One lady commented about not over marinating the meat and she is right. I actually meant to write in the recipe to marinate for 1 to 2 hours and no more than 2. I know lamb chops are an expensive cut of meat and what would be more disappointing than to over marinate and have them too salty. Lastly, if I may suggest to anyone that loves middle-eastern food, I often add 1/8 teaspoon each: cinnamon, allspice and garam masala. They add a delicate flavor that is perfect with the lamb. 
***I tried to submit with no stars and it wouldn't go thru, so I also give them 5 stars!***

I was a little concerned about using vinegar as a marinade here, but took a chance based on the reviews....it was FANTASTIC! We loved these chops and so did our 2 and 5 year old children. They were super-easy to prepare. You HAVE to keep the onions and do this : make a little tray using two layers of aluminum foil. Spray it with cooking spray and place (drained onions) on it and carefully place tray on grill, alongside the chops. We cooked our chops on med-hi for 8 mins. exactly and in that time the onions cooked and carmelized a bit and man, they were tasty. Next time I will at least double the onions, they were that good.
Also, I would not recommend leaving the chops in any longer than the 2 hours stated in the recipe.

I added an 1/8 tsp each cinnamon, all spice and garam masala and loved the flavor. I also doubled the onion and made a tray of oiled aluminum foil for the left over onion. Placed tray on grill and cooked alongside chops. I also sauteed mushrooms and fresh mint in the extra marinade.

I made it and was good. The tang from the vinegar was a pop of flavor. I doubled the recipe and it turned out good.. I cooked longer than the recommended time cause I don't like that much pink in my meat.

After reading the reviews for this recipe, I decided to give it a try and I wasn't disappointed. It was easy to make - I followed Noor's additional suggestion and added garam masala, allspice and cinnamon which gave an excellent flavour. Because I cooked the lamb on an indoor grill, and I wanted to use the onions as had been suggested, I removed the onions from the marinade and put them in a small skillet for about 10 minutes over medium heat to carmalize. I served them over the lamb chops - yummy. Super recipe Noor - and great added suggestion as well.

I loved the marinade! Very easy to make. However, I used Bragg's Organic Apple Cider Vinegar. I found that lining a large casserole dish with foil and letting the lamb chops sit a few minutes let the juices REALLY soak in. They were almost better later. Served with baby carrots and white potatoes, sprayed with olive oil and sprinkled with sea salt, pepper, onion powder, and paprika, wrapped in foil and grilled for 30 minutes. Also..grilled romaine sprayed with olive oil, sprinkled sea salt, black pepper, rosemary, oregano, and garlic powder.

Oops! Got cut off in the middle of my review! I made these with mini potatoes, and cooked everything in the oven at 400 degrees. Removed the chops after 20 minutes and potatoes and onions after 30. I took the marinade and strained it into a small pot, and added about 2 tablespoons of honey. While everything was cooking I reduced it down to a light sauce for the chops. Definitely a winning recipe that is easy to change for personal tastes. I will definitely be making these again!

This recipe was great! I seldom cooked lamb because it always came out tasting “musky”. But I followed these directions, also adding a teaspoon of beef shawarma seasoning to the mix. I let my large lamb chop marinate for 2 hours in the refrigerator. Then I grilled it on my tabletop grill for 8 minutes on each side. ( I like well done meat). Following other reviews, I sautéed onions and mushrooms in a small pan and then added them to the lamb while it was grilling. Absolutely delicious!!! Such an easy and tasty recipe.
Adjusted the marinade to use Balsamic Vinegar rather than white vinegar, added a pinch of Rosemary and an 1/8 t. lemon pepper. The three changes enhanced the flavor; made it more Italian.

Instead of turning on the grill, to save time I tried cooking these in a heavy preheated uncovered aluminum pot in the oven (maybe next time I'll try the pizza stone). Also dumped in some thyme clippings. Turned out well.

Great recipe! I followed it, with the additional spices Noor mentioned in his comment (Garam Masala etc..) and it turned out really well. Great flavor without hiding the natural lamb taste. I broiled in the oven but I imagine they'd be even better on the bbq.
Made the marinade exactly per recipe. The chops were cooked perfectly med-rare, and were perfectly tender! Big hit!

Wow, simple is right! These lamb chops were divine!! Great recipe for beginner cook, lazy cooks and seasoned cooks. The only substitute was I used garlic paste vs minced garlic. A wonderful appetizer or entree with fun side dishes. This was so fun to grill on Easter Sunday!
I made for my family . I only had an hour to marinate the chops and still they were seriously beyond delicious. Making again today!

Easy recipe. This does not compliment the flavor of lamb. Six people who tasted this recipe made similar comments. “OK” and “edible” were probably the best comments. Think olive oil, garlic rosemary, salt and pepper may be the most likely base. Wines that helped were older Merlot and Syrah from Central CA Coast.

So simple and tasty. I left the onions out, but kept everything else as written. I must have had thick lamb chops because mine were on the rare side even when I kept them in longer, but I don’t mind lamb being rare / medium-rare so still happily ate it.
